title: Elastic Load Balancing: spreading traffic

kcs.statement: Elastic Load Balancing spreads incoming traffic across targets in multiple Availability Zones behind a single DNS endpoint, so no single server is a single point of failure.
A load balancer runs health checks on its targets and stops sending traffic to any target that fails them until it passes again.

Application Load Balancer routes HTTP/HTTPS (layer 7) by path or host name. Network Load Balancer handles TCP/UDP (layer 4) at very high throughput with static IP addresses. Gateway Load Balancer (layer 3) sends traffic through third-party virtual appliances such as firewalls.

problem_ideas: An app must send /api/* to one fleet and /images/* to another: which load balancer type?
A trading system needs millions of TCP connections per second and a fixed IP for client allow-lists: which type?
A company must inspect all traffic through a third-party firewall appliance: which type?
Three instances sit in one AZ behind a load balancer and that AZ fails: what went wrong in the design?
One of four targets starts returning HTTP 500 errors: describe what the load balancer does next.
A distractor says a load balancer adds instances when traffic rises: which service actually does that?
